calls.head: Like for like: Bowman vs. Perron
calls.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending Bowman’s line (Lavoie, Dowd and Bowman) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Stars’ fourth line is Blackwell, Faksa and Perron.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Stone sets the Golden Knights’ points record
paras: Miro Heiskanen struck first for the Stars early in the first. Wyatt Johnston stretched the lead to 2-0 midway through the period, his fourth straight game with a goal. Victor Olofsson and William Karlsson scored less than three minutes apart early in the second to tie it 2-2. Jérémy Lauzon gave the Golden Knights the lead early in the third, but Thomas Harley made it 3-3 for Dallas with just over three minutes left. Jason Robertson and Tyler Seguin scored in the shootout for the Stars.

The Golden Knights had a little more of the play and hit two posts, but the Stars won the shootout. Jake Oettinger made 27 saves for the Stars, and Adin Hill stopped 19 of 22 at the other end. The Stars improved to 14-6-2, second in the Central, while the Knights dropped to 13-6-5, second in the Pacific.

items.text: Mark Stone passed Jonathan Marchessault to become the Golden Knights’ all-time leader in points, with 418.
Four straight wins for the Stars.
The Golden Knights are winless in four (0-1-3).
Wyatt Johnston extended his point streak against Vegas to eight games.
